source.name: Official peer-review program registry
source.authority: Publisher, scholarly society, accreditor, and government program pages

records.title: Volunteer to review research software for JOSS
records.why: JOSS publicly invites experienced developers and researchers to review open-source research software through a transparent GitHub-based process.
records.eligibility: Best for people with practical research-software, open-source, testing, documentation, or domain expertise.
records.proof: Public JOSS review and reviewer contribution
records.effort: First review pass in about 2–4 weeks

records.title: Volunteer as an ACM journal reviewer
records.why: ACM directs prospective reviewers to journals in their subject area and invites them to contact the editor-in-chief with relevant expertise.
records.eligibility: Requires subject expertise that fits a specific ACM journal; publications or strong research artifacts improve selection chances.

records.title: Apply to the IEEE Access Associate Editor team
records.deadline: Rolling while the official call remains open
records.why: IEEE Access is accepting qualified volunteers to coordinate rigorous peer review across IEEE fields of interest.
records.eligibility: PhD in a relevant field, significant publication record, and at least ten years of journal publishing experience expected.
records.proof: Associate Editor service and peer-review leadership
records.effort: Coordinate review of about four articles per month

records.title: Register as an HRSA grant reviewer
records.org: U.S. Health Resources and Services Administration
records.why: HRSA recruits healthcare and community experts to score federal grant applications; nonfederal reviewers are compensated.
records.eligibility: Healthcare, health workforce, public health, rural health, or underserved-community knowledge and experience.
records.effort: Training, written scoring, and panel discussion

source.name: HRSA
source.authority: U.S. Health Resources and Services Administration

records.title: Enroll in the NIH Early Career Reviewer Program
records.why: NIH trains eligible early-career scientists through first-hand grant peer-review service and recruits from the resulting reviewer database.
records.eligibility: Doctorate, qualifying independent U.S.-institution research role, recent senior-authored publications, and prior NIH application required; verify every condition.
records.effort: Training plus 7–9 applications and a 1–2 day meeting

records.title: Volunteer to review DOE biological and environmental research proposals
records.org: U.S. Department of Energy Biological and Environmental Research
records.why: DOE BER maintains an official volunteer form for experts interested in independent scientific and technical merit review.
records.eligibility: Relevant scientific expertise and freedom from conflicts of interest; selection depends on each panel's needs.

source.name: DOE Biological and Environmental Research
source.authority: U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science

records.title: Apply to become a Higher Learning Commission peer reviewer
records.why: HLC is accepting applications for trained peer reviewers who evaluate colleges and universities and support institutional improvement.
records.eligibility: Higher-education and accreditation experience; applicants should check HLC's current selection criteria before applying.
